tune._note: Fractions of the CHILD'S OWN range (still level → moving level from the practice). Set by harness runs (still kid vs moving kid) — the CLI replaces these with the values that separate them, and logs old→new with the numbers.
tune._qaNote: provisionalMoveMult/moveFloorMult are QA Q4. When the practice arm-up is missed there is no measured moving level, so the still level is multiplied to invent one. At the old x4 the trick threshold landed at k~1.9 x the child's stillness, and the architect's simulation showed a PERFECTLY STILL child getting a false GOTCHA in 12% of trick windows with 1% keypoint flips, 25% with 3% flips, and 13% when fps dropped 15->8 - the game punishing the child for listening. x10 lands at k~3.7 (0% false GOTCHA in every simulated condition) and moveFloorMult is a hard floor so the threshold can never sit below 3x stillness however the arithmetic falls out. jumpRejectSW is Q6 (a one-frame wrist teleport further than 0.8 shoulder-widths is a detection glitch, not movement). nominalFps converts the pre-calibration provisional thresholds into the per-second units Q5 introduced.

presence._qaNote: maxWaitMs added 2026-09-26 (QA Q2 follow-up): the presence gate had no escape. A founder test stuck on 'I can't see your wrists - step back' because the all-six-joints rule demanded more than the judge needs. The gate now asks for both shoulders + one joint per arm, and continues anyway after this many ms - the spec's own rule is that the game is never stuck.

_capNote: 180 -> 210 by the CLI 2026-09-23. Measured from the real captured clips a full game runs 212s worst-case / 188s with fast answers; at 180 the page's own D5 guard truncates round 3, which is the lightning round. The overrun is structural (step counts + window lengths), not fixable in the audio: a 'Nova says X' line is ~2s at a natural pace and the pack's 1.4s target is not sayable. Revert to 180 if the design would rather drop three steps from round 3.
_bakeNote: Measured on pod 7b5c2clec7ih8w 2026-09-23, not assumed. Every bake is 121 frames = 4.84s @25fps. The gesture peaks at: star 0.72s, clap 2.08s, lefthand 2.48s, righthand 2.64s, bear 3.84s. The pack's 1200-1400ms would have swapped her back to the talk body BEFORE the gesture happened in four of the five — the child would see her twitch and reset. These values are peak+250ms so she is still holding the pose while he copies it. Consequence: a demo now overlaps the response window (bear especially), which the design did not anticipate - the honest fix is faster source clips, re-baked.
_peakNote: peakMs = the measured peak of each bake (bakeMs minus the 250ms hold). Added 2026-09-25 for QA Q1: the demo now starts at the line's START and the judge window opens at windowOpensAtPeakFrac x peak, because children copy what they SEE. Before this the window opened at the line's END, which for clap/left/right/bear was 0.9-2.4s BEFORE her arms reached the pose - real commands missed and a late copier on a trick moved after the window had closed and was scored +2 stars for moving. If the gestures are ever re-baked faster, update peakMs and bakeMs together; every peak under 1.2s is the fix at source and takes the game back under the 210s cap.
_freezeNote: freezeWindowPadS: QA Q3. Freeze needs holdMs (1.0s) of stillness but the EMA energy takes 0.3-0.5s to settle after a child stops, so round 3's 1.6s window could not physically be satisfied. The freeze window is now at least holdMs + 1.2s regardless of the round.
